name: OpenEvolve
one_liner: An open-source take on AlphaEvolve: LLMs mutate programs, your evaluator scores them, and a MAP-Elites and island database keeps diverse winners.

loop.proposes: Code changes in marked EVOLVE-BLOCK regions, written by an ensemble of LLMs from any compatible API
loop.judged_by: A user-written evaluator that scores each program; errors and other evaluator output are kept as artifacts
loop.steers: Scores place programs in a MAP-Elites grid across island populations; errors and evaluator output feed the next prompt

headline_result: The project reports 2-3x speedups on GPU kernels (MLX Metal) and a circle packing for n=26 that its README calls state of the art, plus sorting and signal-processing examples. These are the project's own claims; the README gives no numeric circle-packing score.
caveat: All results are project-reported and not independently replicated here. The README gives no numbers for most examples. It is an engineering framework, not a paper.
beyond_harness_note: The evolutionary loop with its MAP-Elites and island database does the search, and the evolved program is a plain artifact usable without the model.
generative_model: Pluggable LLM ensemble, frozen (any OpenAI-compatible API or supported CLI)

verification.notes: Read the upstream README: MAP-Elites, islands with migration, LLM ensembles, artifact feedback, Apache-2.0. Confirmed via HTTP 301 that github.com/codelion/openevolve redirects to algorithmicsuperintelligence/openevolve (GitHub API: created 2025-05-15). The draft said 'sorting, circle packing, kernel optimization' - README mentions adaptive sorting, signal processing, circle packing n=26 and MLX Metal kernels (2-3x). No paper to cite; evidence level is code. Third-party description of the MAP-Elites/island design also appears in ThetaEvolve (arXiv:2511.23473), not opened in full.
